requirements.statement: For each link that has a visible label (text shown on screen within the link, or an image of text), the link's accessible name contains at least that visible label.

citations.quote: Pour chaque lien ayant un intitulé visible, le nom accessible du lien contient-il au moins l’intitulé visible (hors cas particuliers) ?
Texte affiché faisant office d’intitulé visible à l’écran au sein d’un bouton ou d’un lien.
Ce texte peut être constitué de texte ou d’une image contenant du texte.

routes.statement: The accessible name contains the visible label as an exact string, at its start or elsewhere, possibly with other words added.

citations.quote: le nom accessible du lien contient-il au moins l’intitulé visible
WCAG insiste sur le placement de l’intitulé visible au début du nom accessible sans toutefois réserver l’exclusivité de cet emplacement ;
WCAG considère comme un cas d’échec une correspondance non exacte de la chaîne de caractères de l’intitulé visible au sein du nom accessible.

exceptions.statement: Punctuation and capital letters of the visible label may be left out of the accessible name.

citations.quote: La ponctuation et les lettres majuscules sont présentes dans le texte de l’intitulé visible : elles peuvent être ignorées dans le nom accessible sans porter à conséquence ;

exceptions.statement: When the visible label's text serves as a symbol, the accessible name expresses the function the symbol conveys instead of the literal text; a mathematical expression may still be taken up literally.

citations.quote: Le texte de l’intitulé visible sert de symbole : le texte ne doit pas être interprété littéralement au niveau du nom accessible. Le nom doit exprimer la fonction véhiculée par le symbole
si l’étiquette visible représente une expression mathématique, les symboles mathématiques peuvent être repris littéralement pour servir d’étiquette au nom accessible

requirements.statement: For each link whose visible label comes with a title attribute (for an SVG link, a title element or an xlink:title attribute), the content of that title contains the visible label.

citations.quote: Pour chaque lien, vérifier que le contenu de l’attribut `title` ou de l’attribut `aria-label` ou de l’attribut `aria-labelledby` contient l’intitulé visible ;

Pour chaque lien SVG, vérifier que le contenu de l’attribut `aria-labelledby` ou de l’attribut `aria-label` ou de l’élément `<title>` ou de l’attribut `x-link:title` ou d’un ou plusieurs éléments `<text>` contient l’intitulé visible ;

routes.statement: The title's content contains the visible label.

citations.quote: Pour chaque lien, vérifier que le contenu de l’attribut `title` ou de l’attribut `aria-label` ou de l’attribut `aria-labelledby` contient l’intitulé visible ;

rationale.text: The wording asks that a link's accessible name contain at least its visible label, with two particular cases: punctuation and capitals may be ignored, and a visible text that serves as a symbol is named by its function. The methodology also checks a link's title attribute (or an SVG link's title or xlink:title) against the visible label, and the glossary of the link label says a title that does not take up the name from content makes the label non-explicit; this is kept as a second requirement, with the same particular cases, and no check is linked to it. Deciding the test in general is judgment: whether a text serves as a symbol, and which displayed text or image of text acts as the label. The candidate is none. The custom check examines HTML links whose name comes from a non-empty aria-label, builds an inventory V of the link's visible text, and faults when no word of V appears in the name. Its fault is evidence only, because the inventory can compare the wrong text. The glossary scopes the label to text displayed on screen, and the check's inventory misses two ways the displayed text can differ from the DOM text. It excludes generated ::before and ::after content but does not look at ::marker, and it measures the text's paint with the computed color without checking -webkit-text-fill-color. Codex showed this in a browser: a link displayed as a list item with an inside marker whose content is « Open account », aria-label « Open account », and a child span « Hidden fallback » with an opaque computed colour but a transparent text fill. The browser displays « Open account », which matches the name; the check takes « Hidden fallback » as V, finds none of its words in the name, and faults. The link keeps its routes and its partial scope and becomes evidence_only. It never answered no_fault. What would raise the entry: a check that establishes the displayed label and the computed accessible name, abstaining on any generated label it does not read (::marker included) and on any text paint that makes its inventory unsure (transparent or differing text fill, text stroke and the like), with the marker and transparent-text fixture beside a genuinely disjoint plain label. A resolving rule for which text is the visible label and when it is a symbol is still not given by the text. axe's label-content-name-mismatch compares the visible text of elements labelled through aria-label or aria-labelledby with their name. Its exact normalisation and handling of symbols are not known here, it also examines buttons and other widgets, and it ignores title attributes and images of text, so it is evidence only, partial, for the first route. Applicability is judgment: whether a link has a visible label can need judgment, as for an image of text. Needs is empty.
